summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and a history of anxiety and depression was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diabetic ketoacidosis. She presented with elevated blood glucose, an anion gap of 21, and hypertensive urgency with systolic blood pressure up to 210, which resolved with treatment. She was managed with an insulin drip, IV fluids, and antiemetics, and transitioned to subcutaneous insulin as her condition improved. Anxiety was addressed with Ativan and continuation of citalopram, with psychiatry support. Her diet was advanced as nausea resolved, and she stabilized over five days. She was discharged home with instructions to use Ativan for early anxiety or nausea, continue her medications including increased metoclopramide, and follow up with her PCP, diabetes team, and a psychiatrist. A social work referral was made for ongoing support.
